title: Template abilities need ability_type or subtype to route to correct container
description:
Template abilities (in changes[].abilities) need a field indicating which stat block container they belong to. The 5 containers are:

1. senses.special_senses (subtype=special_sense) — Darkvision, low-light vision
2. defense.automatic_abilities (ability_type=automatic) — auras, constant abilities  
3. defense.reactive_abilities (ability_type=reactive) — reactions
4. offense.offensive_actions — attacks, offensive abilities
5. interaction_abilities (ability_type=interaction) — interaction abilities

Plus: defense.hitpoints[*].automatic_abilities — HP-level abilities like fast healing

Currently Ghost template has Darkvision with subtype=ability, but it needs subtype=special_sense to route to senses.special_senses. Similarly, Negative Healing should route to defense.automatic_abilities and Ghostly Passage should route based on its ability_type.

The add_items effects specify multiple targets (one per container), and the engine needs to know which abilities go where. Either:
a) Set ability_type/subtype on each ability to match the target container, or
b) Add a filter field on each add_items effect to select which abilities to add

title: Template effect paths don't match stat_block structure for skills/languages
description: Template effects use paths like $.skills[*].value and $.languages.languages but in the actual creature JSON, skills lives at $.statistics.skills and languages at $.statistics.languages. The stat_block root has: creature_type, sources, senses, statistics, defense, offense. Skills and languages are nested under statistics. Templates should use $.statistics.skills[*].value and $.statistics.languages.languages.

title: Fix sentence fragments parsed as trait names in monster templates
description: Several templates have text sentences split into individual trait add_items instead of actual trait names. Examples: Skeleton adds 'Undead Traits And', 'Optionally', 'The Mindless'. Water element adds 'Water Trait', 'Either The Amphibious Or Aquatic'. Undead template adds 'Undead Trait' (with suffix). These should be actual trait names like 'Undead', 'Mindless', 'Water', 'Amphibious', 'Aquatic'.
notes:
Partially fixed in commit 6c77fda3c. 5 fragments remain across 3 templates:
- Skeleton: 'Undead Traits And', 'The Mindless' (should be 'Undead', optionally 'Mindless')
- Undead: 'Undead Trait' (should be 'Undead')
- Water: 'Water Trait', 'Either The Amphibious Or Aquatic' (should be 'Water', and either 'Amphibious' or 'Aquatic')

title: Fix movement_type 'land' → 'walk' in template effects
description: Templates (Dwarf, Elf, Merfolk, Amphibious) reference movement_type=='land' in JSONPath filters, but creature data uses 'walk' for walking speed. The filter [?(@.movement_type=='land')] never matches. Change to 'walk'.
close_reason: Fixed: movement_type 'land' → 'walk' via _normalize_movement_type in enrichment extractor

title: Monster family: preserve section text when building changes/subtypes
description:
When parsing monster families (e.g., Lich, Ghoul), the parser currently consumes section content to build monster_family.changes and monster_family.subtypes, leaving the original sections empty. This means the display can't render the full family content from sections alone.

Two things need to be preserved in sections:

1. **Section text**: The descriptive text for each section/subsection (e.g., 'Creating a Lich' rules text, 'Lich Abilities' description)

2. **Section abilities**: The abilities within each subsection must remain in the sections tree. The display uses these to:
   - Render family abilities in collapsible sections (already works for Ghoul family's 'Creating Ghouls' subsections)
   - Match creature abilities that have no text with their family counterpart. e.g., Ghast's 'Consume Flesh' and 'Ghast Fever' abilities have no text on the creature — they reference the family's version. The display needs to find the matching ability in the family sections to show its description.

Without both text AND abilities preserved in sections, the display falls back to showing empty or incomplete family content.

**Current state:**
- Lich family: 'Creating a Lich' section has text but no abilities/subsections. All content consumed into monster_family.changes[] and monster_family.subtypes[]
- Ghoul family: 'Creating Ghouls' section has nested subsections BUT their abilities lists are empty — consumed into monster_family data
- The display's Sections component already renders sections with nested abilities (works when data is present)

**What the display needs:** The section tree should be the complete source of truth for rendering. The monster_family.changes/subtypes can coexist for the template engine, but sections must not be stripped.

Two options:
**Option A (preferred by display):** Keep sections intact with full text + abilities. Also produce changes/subtypes for the engine.
**Option B:** If the parser intentionally strips sections, explain how pfsrd2-display should render monster_family.changes and monster_family.subtypes.
close_reason: Sections now preserve text and abilities. Subtypes reference via JSONPath. 0 errors on full run.

title: Monster family Military (ID 543): ability in ul/li change list
description: The Military NPC family has a Pounce ability with <span class='action'> embedded inside a <ul><li> change list item. The ability parser doesn't extract abilities from within <li> elements. The <li> says 'Add the Pounce ability' and defines Pounce inline. Need to either: extract abilities from <li> text in change lists, or restructure the HTML.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #94 — Pounce moved out of li, adjustments detection added

title: Monster family Dragon Resurrection (ID 587): orphaned traits/span in section text
description: The Dragon Resurrection 'Alternate Abilities' h3 section has ability text (traits + action span) leaking into the section text after h3 body split. The 'Shred Souls' ability's (divine, void) traits and [free-action] span end up orphaned because the h3 split breaks the text mid-ability. Needs investigation — may be an HTML structure issue or a content filter ordering problem.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #94 — h4 headings added, traits-before-action extraction order

title: 5 monster families need HTML structure fixes for section hierarchy
description:
5 monster families fail with the unified ability parser because their HTML has broken heading hierarchies — h2/h3 headings are embedded inside section text instead of creating proper section boundaries.

Failing files:
- ID 68 (Lich): h3 'Lich Abilities' contains h3.framing source headers ('Book of the Dead') that get promoted to h2 after the h3 was already processed
- ID 291 (Graveknight): Same pattern — h3 'Graveknight Abilities' with embedded source headers
- ID 315 (Mana Wastes Mutant): Abilities with action spans in descriptive text
- ID 543 (Military): Ability embedded in ul/li change list  
- ID 587 (Dragon Resurrection): span in section text

Root cause: the content filter's h3 unwrap logic doesn't account for nested heading hierarchies. These need either HTML fixes or a more sophisticated content filter that properly handles headings within headings.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #94 — HTML template leaks fixed, content filter simplified

title: Monster family: expand creation section detection beyond 'creating'/'building'
description: The _extract_creation_changes function in monster_family.py only recognizes sections with 'creating' or 'building' in the name as creation sections. Many families have creation-type sections with different names like 'Shape-Changing Dragons', 'Imperial Dragon Spellcasters', 'Alternate Abilities', 'Alternate Graveknight Abilities', etc. These sections contain construction instructions (how to modify a creature) but aren't detected as creation sections. Need a broader detection heuristic or an explicit list of creation-section patterns.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #94 — _is_creation_section expanded to match abilities, spellcasters, adjustments

title: Monster family sections: parse addons and afflictions as structured data
description:
Monster family sections like 'Creating Ghouls' contain abilities that need proper structured parsing, not just flat ability lists.

Two issues:

1. **Afflictions parsed as separate abilities**: Ghast Fever/Ghoul Fever in the Ghoul family are split into individual abilities per line ('Ghast Fever', 'Saving Throw', 'Stage 1', 'Stage 2', etc.). These should be parsed as affliction objects with structured saving_throw and stages fields, matching how afflictions are parsed in creature stat blocks. The pattern is recognizable: ability followed by 'Saving Throw' then 'Stage N' entries.

2. **Addon abilities not parsed as structured types**: Family section abilities like Consume Flesh ('[one-action] As ghoul...') have action costs embedded in the text field instead of being parsed into action_type fields. Similarly, traits like '(disease)', '(incapacitation, occult, necromancy)' are in the text instead of being parsed as trait arrays. These should match the structured format used in creature stat block abilities (action_type, traits, trigger, effect, etc.).

Affected families: Ghoul (confirmed), likely others with 'Creating X' template sections.

Related: pfsrd2-5l0 (Ghast Fever stages), pfsrd2-rtu (text leaked into name)
close_reason: Fixed in PR #94 — unified ability parser handles addons, traits, actions, afflictions for monster family abilities

title: Ghoul family: Ghast Fever parsed as separate abilities per stage
description: In the Ghoul monster family 'Ghast Abilities' section, Ghast Fever has been split into individual abilities for each component: 'Ghast Fever' (disease), 'Saving Throw' Fortitude, 'Stage 1', 'Stage 2', etc. These should be a single affliction entry (or at minimum a single ability) with the saving throw and stages as structured data, matching how afflictions are parsed in creature stat blocks. Same issue likely affects Ghoul Fever in the 'Ghoul Abilities' section.

title: Ghoul family: Ghast Abilities section has empty text, content leaked into name
description: In the Ghoul monster family, the 'Ghast Abilities' subsection under 'Creating Ghouls' has its descriptive text ('A ghast has all the abilities above, plus following additions.') concatenated into the section name instead of being in the text field. The text field is empty. Section name should be just 'Ghast Abilities' with the rest in the text field. Similarly check 'Ghoul Abilities' section for the same pattern.

title: Template abilities change text should use line breaks between ability names
description: The abilities change text in monster templates concatenates ability names and descriptions into a single line. e.g. Ghost template: '- Add the following abilities.  **Darkvision**  **Negative Healing**  **Ghostly Passage** [one-action] The creature Flies and...' Each ability should be on its own line (separated by newlines) so renderers can display them as a list. The structured abilities[] array has the correct data, but the text field is used for the human-readable description and should be formatted with line breaks between abilities.

title: Ghost template: replace_highest_with speed missing fly item
description: The speed change effect uses replace_highest_with but has no item field defining the fly speed replacement. The engine checks eff.Item != nil and skips the operation. Need to add the fly speed item to the effect data.

title: Ghost template: weakness names include descriptive prefix
description: Weakness item names contain 'with a value based on the creature\'s level: force' instead of just 'force'. The descriptive text should be in the change description, not the item name.

title: Ghost template: weakness conditionals have gaps (levels 5-8, 10-13)
description: The Ghost template weakness effects only have conditionals for levels <=3, ==4, ==9, >=14. Levels 5-8 and 10-13 fall through with no weakness added. Need conditionals covering all level ranges per the PF2e Ghost template table.

title: Extract canonical source name lookup table
description: The game_id hash depends on exact source name strings (book name, page, entry name). Spelling, capitalization, punctuation, or extraneous words in source names will produce different hashes and break game_id consistency across parsers. Need a canonical source name registry that normalizes source names so any parser can look up the correct canonical form before generating a game_id. This prevents broken IDs from typos or formatting differences between data sources.

title: Ghost template: magical trait not added to physical Strikes
description: Per PF2e Ghost template rules, physical Strikes should gain the magical trait. The template data has no effect adding traits to attacks.

value: Unified ability parser (PFSRD2-Parser-90ev): Phase 1 in progress on branch feature/unified-ability-parser. universal/ability.py created with parse_abilities_from_nodes and parse_ability_from_html. 20 tests passing. Monster family wired up but 8 failures due to: (1) action spans in non-creation section text, (2) schema missing 'damage' field on ability. Content filter no longer unwraps spans - this surfaced pre-existing issues. Monster template not yet wired up. Stashed Phase 2 ability-placement work on feature/ability-placement-from-enrichment.
